title: Derived morphism sheaves evaluate on weakly contractible pro-etale affines
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $B$ a finite commutative ring, and $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $E\in D(B)$ be bounded with finite $B$-module cohomology, and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ be bounded with finite locally constant cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\underline E$ for its constant sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $\mathcal H_{E,K}$ and $\mathcal I_{E,K}$ by sheafifying, on the etale site, the presheaves $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ and $V\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every affine object $U\to X$ weakly contractible for $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is surjective on sections over $U$, there are canonical bijections
$$
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal H_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U),\qquad
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal I_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Isom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U).
$$
Here restriction is to the localized pro-etale site over $U$, identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The bijections extend pullback of actual etale-local morphisms, preserve identity morphisms and composition whenever defined, and are natural in $E,K$ and restriction between such objects. For a homomorphism $B\to C$ of finite commutative rings for which $E_C=E\otimes_B^L C$ and $K_C=K\otimes_B^L C$ remain bounded with the corresponding finite cohomology hypotheses, they commute with derived scalar extension: the map of pulled-back morphism or isomorphism sheaves induced by $f\mapsto f\otimes_B^L C$ evaluates to the same operation on actual derived morphisms. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

proof.text: The exact constant-sheaf derived functor preserves boundedness and commutes with each homology functor. A constant sheaf of a finite module is finite locally constant: the constant trivialization gives local constancy, and the geometric stalk of a constant sheaf is the module itself. Transfer these properties across the homology comparison isomorphism to the constant derived source.

source.place: Exact constant functor, geometric constant stalk and derived homology comparison

proof.text: Apply the bounded finite locally constant Hom-comparison lemma to all four ordered pairs among the constant source and K. Both objects are bounded, hence bounded below as targets. Apply the fully proved inverse-pair Isom comparison lemma to these four Hom isomorphisms.

source.place: Parent argument steps 1-5 and 7-9, isolated into the two comparison lemmas

proof.text: The weakly contractible pro-etale sheafification units are bijective by the existing comparison interface. Each evaluation is the component of its now invertible comparison followed by the inverse of this bijection. Its two factors are bijective, proving the simultaneous Hom and Isom assertion.

source.place: Weakly contractible unit bijectivity and definition of both evaluation maps

proof.text: For composition, identify comparison on actual local maps using the two adjunction units. Sheafification extensionality on binary products and the inverse-image product comparison extend functorial preservation of composition from these generators to arbitrary sheaf sections. Cancel the injective pro-etale sheafification unit to prove the Hom and Isom evaluation composition formulas. Retain the already proved local extension, restriction, identity and naturality proofs.

source.place: Actual local-map comparison, binary-product sheafification and functor laws

proof.text: Use the coherent localized scalar-extension construction for T,S,c and their normalized adjunctions. Transpose its equality on actual local Hom maps twice to prove the Hom comparison square after sheafification and comparison inverse image. The same equality on forward maps proves the Isom square by Iso.ext. Naturality of the pro-etale sheafification units and their injectivity identify these squares with the displayed Hom and Isom evaluation formulas. This is an actual proof of the evaluation compatibility from the local construction, with no tensor base-change claim for internal Hom.

tool_uses.why: K-injective restriction on any ringed-site slice supplies the resolutions used in steps 4 and 8; this unit has no slice-resolution substitute.
Global derived Hom is hypercohomology of internal Hom, applied on the two sites and their slices; this is generic ringed-site infrastructure absent from this unit.
Exact restriction preserves representatives and quasi-isomorphisms on slices; this unit has no replacement for that foundational operation.
Identifies the site slice at an arbitrary weakly etale object with its own pro-etale site and constant coefficients; this unit has no such localization theorem.
Supplies K-injective representatives of arbitrary complexes of module sheaves on small ringed sites; this unit has no resolution-existence theorem.
Exact sheafification for fixed-ring module presheaves makes the constant-module functor exact in step 1; a generic sheafification tool, not a replacement for any proper-base-change route step.
